high.title: Korean Won Worst Performer Among Asian Peers, Tests New Crisis-Era Low of 1,550
high.summary: The Korean won has reached crisis levels, trading above 1,500 against the USD despite South Korea's record current account surplus and upgraded growth expectations. The Bank of Korea is expected to raise rates at least twice to 3.0% this year to combat inflation, with Governor Shin Hyun-song facing mounting pressure as the currency defies traditional economic fundamentals. Deputy Governor Yoo Sang-dae's recent comments have jolted bond markets and heightened expectations of a monetary policy turning point. For FX traders, this presents a critical juncture where fundamentals and technicals diverge - the won's weakness against strong macro indicators suggests potential BOK intervention or more aggressive rate hikes ahead. Watch for 1,550 as a key psychological resistance level.

high.title: USD-KRW Surges Over 25 Won on US Nonfarm Payrolls Shock, Hits Mid-1,550s
high.summary: The USD-KRW exploded higher by over 25 won during extended trading, breaking decisively above 1,550 to reach 1,555.00 - the highest level since March 2009. This surge followed strong US nonfarm payrolls data that reduced Fed easing expectations while Korean markets suffered massive foreign outflows. The move represents a critical technical break that could trigger BOK intervention or emergency policy measures. For bond investors, this level threatens financial stability and may force the central bank's hand on rates or FX intervention. The timing coincides with record foreign equity selling, creating a perfect storm for won weakness that challenges the BOK's policy framework.

high.title: Dollar-Won Breaches 1,560 Mark as Fear Contagion Spreads from US Chip Stock Rout
high.summary: The won collapse accelerated overnight, with USD-KRW hitting 1,559.00 - a 29.30 won surge from Seoul close as panic selling intensified following the US semiconductor rout. The move represents contagion fears that Korean chip giants will follow US tech stocks lower, triggering massive capital flight. This level approaches the 1,600 psychological barrier last seen during the global financial crisis, suggesting potential systemic risk. For traders, this represents a critical moment where technical levels give way to panic - intervention probability rises exponentially above 1,550, making this a high-risk environment for position sizing.

medium.title: Foreign Sell-off Sparks Kospi 'Black Friday'; Funds Exit Ahead of SpaceX IPO
medium.summary: The KOSPI suffered a "Black Friday" rout with the won approaching 1,550 per dollar amid massive foreign selling. The selloff reflects capital flight ahead of high-profile IPOs like SpaceX, draining liquidity from Korean markets and pressuring both equities and currency simultaneously.

medium.title: Foreigners Stage W7 Trillion 'Exit' from KOSPI - Largest Single-Day Selloff This Year
medium.summary: Foreign investors dumped nearly 7 trillion won of Korean equities on June 4th, marking the largest single-day selloff of 2026. Year-to-date foreign selling has reached 115.97 trillion won, creating sustained pressure on both the KOSPI and won exchange rate.

medium.title: Korean Chips Plunge Despite Jensen Huang Visit - KOSPI Retreats Below 8,100
medium.summary: The KOSPI plunged 5.54% to 8,160.59 despite NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang's visit, as US semiconductor weakness triggered massive selling. Foreigners sold 3.52 trillion won while the won-dollar rate hit 1,539.10, threatening key technical levels.

medium.title: Dollar-Won Trades in Early 1,530s in New York Session
medium.summary: USD-KRW traded at 1,532.00 during NY hours, up 15.60 won from the previous session, showing continued weakness pressure on the Korean currency across global trading sessions.

medium.title: NH Investment & Securities Bond Offering Draws KRW 2 Trillion in Orders
medium.summary: NH Investment & Securities raised KRW 300 billion via corporate bonds with 7x oversubscription (KRW 2.1 trillion orders). 2-year notes priced below fair value while 5-year bonds showed weakness, indicating curve steepening pressure amid rate uncertainty.

medium.title: US Treasuries Rally on Israel-Lebanon Ceasefire Agreement
medium.summary: US 10-year Treasury yields fell 3.40bp to 4.457% on ceasefire news between Israel and Lebanon, reducing geopolitical risk premiums and supporting bond prices globally.
